transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-09-14   Start: 15:02 UTC   Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Li (Nova CTO), Sarah Gomez (Nova Platform Eng), Maya Patel (Nova InfoSec)
Recording: yes

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Tom: yeah loud and clear thanks Alex. we invited Sarah and Maya cause this is partly platform and partly security.
[00:10] Alex: great, i'll do a 5 minute intro then priya will take the integration questions. quick goal — understand your integration surface and constraints for hosted -> dedicated -> private.
[00:20] Tom: perfect, we're evaluating options for an LLM gateway to power routing for payment fraud detection and customer support generation. main Qs: how do we integrate with existing sdk stacks, any LangChain / LlamaIndex support, and how do rate limits and observability work?
[00:34] Priya: awesome. quick background on Redwood: hosted api is easiest to start, dedicated for predictable throughput, and private if you need VPC/on-prem. we provide SDKs (python/js/go), plus example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex.
[00:47] Sarah: can you share the LangChain example now? like embedding + rerank flows — we use embeddings heavily for semantic search.
[00:55] Priya: yes, i'll send the repo after. we have a short sample where LangChain calls the Redwood python client for embeddings and then LlamaIndex for doc indexing. it's basically same as OpenAI adapter but with small differences in streaming and chunked batching.
[01:12] Maya: security first — does your hosted route allow us to bring our own KMS, or is that only for private deployments?
[01:18] Alex: BYOK for KMS is available for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we offer encrypted at rest and in transit, but customer-managed KMS is enterprise-only via Dedicated/private.
[01:29] Maya: ok makes sense. we need SOC2 + audit logs and fine-grained RBAC.
[01:34] Priya: we support audit logs, SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning and role-based access. audit logs are available in Redwood Console and can be exported to S3 or your SIEM.
[01:45] Tom: great. now about deployment topology — we currently have an internal API gateway (kong + envoy) and want Redwood to sit behind our gateway as a proxy. can we do that?
[01:57] Priya: yes, two common patterns — 1) direct SDK calls from backend services to Redwood hosted api with the gateway just proxying traffic and applying auth headers; 2) run a small sidecar/ingress proxy that handles retries, rate limiting, and key rotation and then forwards to Redwood. for Dedicated/private you can also terminate inside your VPC.
[02:18] Sarah: if we put a proxy in front, can Redwood propagate trace headers (x-request-id / traceparent) so our observability links requests end-to-end?
[02:27] Priya: absolutely — we pass through traceparent, and have integration hooks for Datadog and Honeycomb. we also emit per-request metadata in the console (model, tokens, latency, route) and you can stream traces to your tracing endpoint.
[02:40] Tom: rate limiting — how does Redwood handle multi-tenant quotas? we want per-customer and per-route quotas and burst protection.
[02:50] Priya: on Hosted we enforce rate limits at the API key level with tiered quotas; you can set per-route limits via the console or the management api. Dedicated gives you more headroom and custom quota rules, and in Private you can fully enforce quotas via your gateway + Redwood policy engine. we also have token-based billing and token ceilings to protect spend.
[03:14] Tom: is it possible to do soft-limits — like alert and then hard-limit?
[03:19] Priya: yes — alerts + soft-limits are supported. we emit usage webhooks and you can hook to a pager or slack. soft-limit behavior is configurable: warn at x% then block at y%.
[03:30] Maya: on data residency — we process some PII in embeddings, do you offer region pinning?
[03:36] Alex: yes region pinning and dedicated regional pools for Dedicated/private. Hosted has multiple regions but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:45] Tom: latency is important for fraud workflows — we need sub-200ms median for short prompts and under 500ms p95. do you have benchmark numbers?
[03:55] Priya: we publish performance profiles per model and can run a micro-benchmark with your prompt shapes. typical hosted latency varies by model; dedicated with optimized batching and KV cache can meet your p95 targets for small prompts. we'll run a benchmark as part of pilot.
[04:12] Sarah: how do we integrate with LangChain or LlamaIndex retries and streaming? our current stack expects incremental tokens for progressive UI updates.
[04:20] Priya: Redwood supports streaming responses at the SDK level; our LangChain adapter supports the streaming callback interface, and LlamaIndex can pull partial responses as well. small caveat: some community adapters assume OpenAI's event structure; our adapter maps to that but you might see minor differences in metadata fields — we'll share migration notes.
[04:41] Tom: billing — we have a cost target. is there tooling to estimate tokens and cost per route?
[04:48] Alex: console shows token-level cost breakdowns per route and model. Redwood Optimize also suggests batching and quantization to reduce unit cost. for Dedicated we provide committed capacity pricing and burst options.
[05:01] Maya: legal — does Redwood sign DPA and support standard security questionnaires?
[05:06] Alex: yes we have standard DPA and can run through your security questionnaire. we also support contract language for data handling in Dedicated / Private.
[05:15] Sarah: earlier you mentioned gateway/proxy examples — can you sketch recommended headers and a sample config?
[05:21] Priya: sure — recommended flow: your gateway injects x-api-key or mTLS client certs for auth, preserve traceparent, set x-cust-id for per-tenant routing if you want per-customer quotas. sample envoy config we use in the repo handles retries, exponential backoff, and maps 429->retry-after. i'll attach that.
[05:40] Tom: any known gotchas migrating from OpenAI sdk?
[05:44] Priya: mostly minor differences: streaming event envelope, rate limit header names, and slightly different model names. also our batch endpoints for embeddings are more explicit — we recommend testing with your 90th percentile batch size.
[05:58] Maya: do you have an SLA for hosted?
[06:01] Alex: hosted has best-effort, but Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. SLA language will be in the contract.
[06:09] Tom: ok cool. from our side next steps are to see pricing and a short integration example using LangChain + LlamaIndex behind our envoy gateway, then run a small benchmark.
[06:21] Alex: noted. priya, anything to add?
[06:23] Priya: i'll share the repo and a one-pager on proxy patterns. i'll also propose times for the deep technical session.
[06:31] Tom: one more Q — observability hooks: do you emit per-token metrics or just per-request?
[06:36] Priya: currently we emit per-request metrics (tokens, latency, model). we also have sampling for per-token logs in Dedicated for troubleshooting long context runs.
[06:48] Sarah: that sampling option would help debugging.
[06:50] Alex: great — sounds like alignment. i'll send pricing + sizing spreadsheet. thanks everyone.
[06:55] Tom: thanks all, bye.

POST-MEETING RECAP:
- Outcome: Nova interested in POC starting with Hosted for quick integration, moving to Dedicated for residency and SLA during pilot.
- Shared artifacts: pricing worksheet (link: https://redwood.example/pricing/CRM-NOVA-4492), LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples), envoy proxy config snippet (attached in follow-up email).

NOTES ON TRANSCRIPTION: occasional mislabels and minor filler words preserved.
